newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Founders of new Albania communist party pardoned.
newsitem.headline: Founders of new Albania communist party pardoned.

text.p: Albanian President Sali Berisha has pardoned two men jailed for founding a new communist party, which has been banned in the former Stalinist state, an Albanian newspaper reported on Saturday.
The daily Albania on Saturday published for the first time the full list of Berisha's decree last month pardoning or reducing the jail sentences of 102 prisoners.
Last September a Tirana court jailed Timoshenko Pekmezi, 54, for two years and Sami Meta, 62, for 2-1/2 years on charges of founding a communist party and conspiring to overthrow the government.

The daily also said Berisha cut by five years a 15-year sentence on Lenka Cuko, a former senior communist official, who was found guilty of crimes against humanity for deporting dissidents into internal exile.
Popular protests overthrew the hardline communist regime six years ago. A reformist communist government lost a general election in 1992 to Berisha's Democratic Party.

The Socialist Party, heirs to the communists, said last Monday that Berisha had also cut by six months a jail sentence imposed on Socialist leader Fatos Nano in 1994 on charges of embezzlement during his brief term as prime minister in 1991. Nano has about 18 months of his sentence left to serve.
